t: Palmyra grew from a desert caravan station into a leading trading city in the first and second centuries CE, wealthy enough to build the Temple of Bel, the Great Colonnade and the tower tombs.
In the 260s King Odaenathus defeated the Sasanian emperor Shapur I, and his widow Zenobia ruled as regent for her son and rebelled against Rome until Aurelian defeated her and razed the city in 273.
The city shrank to a fortress, then a small village; Timur destroyed it in 1400, and in 1932 the villagers were moved to a new village so that the ancient site could be excavated.
dyk: At its height, around 270 in the reign of Zenobia, Palmyra had more than 200,000 residents, and by the beginning of the 20th century the village on the site had 6,000.
ev: Puzur-Ishtar the Tadmorean agrees to a contract at an Assyrian trading colony at Kultepe, the city's first appearance in the record
The Temple of Bel is dedicated
Hadrian visits, names the city Hadriane Palmyra and makes it a free city
Odaenathus defeats Shapur I near the Euphrates and becomes the ruler of a de facto allied kingdom
Aurelian razes the city after a rebellion
The Rashidun Caliphate takes the city under Khalid ibn al-Walid
Timur attacks and destroys the city, reducing it to a small village
The villagers are moved to the new village of Tadmur and the ancient site is opened to excavation

f.founded: Settlement near the Efqa spring is dated to the Neolithic, with stone tools of about 7500 BCE; the city entered the written record around 2000 BCE, and a legend attributed its founding to Solomon.
f.where: In an oasis of the Syrian Desert in central Syria, 215 km north-east of Damascus, between two mountain ranges and beside the wadi al-Qubur and the Efqa spring.
f.known: Caravan trade between the Silk Road and the Mediterranean; the Temple of Bel; the Great Colonnade; tower tombs and funerary busts; King Odaenathus and Queen Zenobia; the Palmyrene Empire; its razing by Aurelian in 273
f.today: The ancient site is a ruin beside the town of Tadmur, to which the villagers were moved in 1932, and it was declared a World Heritage Site in 1980.
